DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 5) Christian Conduct

Q1. Why did Paul pray that the believers in Ephesus would receive the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him?
A. Because they needed to know what was theirs in Christ in order to take full advantage of those provisions.
B. Because they had faith in Christ but had not yet received the spiritual blessings available to those who believe.
C. Because their love unto all the saints showed that they were growing, but they still needed to become faithful in Christ Jesus.
D. Because revelation knowledge was what would give them the inheritance that had not yet been provided in Christ.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson says Paul prayed for their understanding because knowing what was theirs in Christ enabled them to benefit from those provisions.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [02:25]–[03:17] (approximate range)

Q2. What does Jeremiah 31 specifically establish about the new covenant?
A. It would renew the covenant God made with their fathers while giving them greater ability to obey it.
B. It would add new instructions to the covenant that was made when God brought their fathers out of Egypt.
C. It is not according to the covenant God made with their fathers.
D. It would preserve the old covenant while placing its requirements in their hearts.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson emphasizes that Jeremiah describes a new covenant, not one identical to the covenant made with the fathers.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [11:09]–[12:53] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Jeremiah 31 | Also cited in lesson segment: Hebrews 8

Q3. According to Romans 6:6 as taught, what happened to the old man?
A. He was gradually weakened as the believer learned more about Christ.
B. He was crucified with Christ.
C. He was removed when the believer began to mortify the deeds of the body.
D. He remains present but no longer has any spiritual relevance.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson teaches that the old man was crucified with Christ.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [25:54]–[28:20] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 6:6

Q4. A believer says, "This temptation strengthened me, so God sent it for my growth." What's your response based on the lesson?
A. Temptation can produce growth, but only when God directly allows it for that purpose.
B. God can use what the enemy meant for evil without being the one who tempted the believer.
C. If temptation produces growth, the source is no longer important.
D. God may send temptation when He knows the believer is ready to turn it into spiritual growth.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes God using a temptation for good from God being the one who tempts.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS III — [06:06]–[07:47] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: James 1:3; James 1:2; James 1:12

Q5. A believer keeps falling in the same environment but says, "Next time I will try harder." What needs attention?
A. His determination, because repeated failure shows that his desire has not become strong enough.
B. His structure, because good intention in the same system may keep producing the same outcome.
C. His spiritual experience, because practical structures cannot replace the work of the Spirit.
D. His accountability, because another person can change him.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson recommends changing the structure or environment rather than relying only on stronger determination.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS IV — [01:08]–[04:06] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Timothy 2; James 1

Q6. Which accountability response conflicts most with Galatians 6:1 as used in the Lesson?
A. Noticing a pattern the person has become unable to see.
B. Intervening when the person insists that nothing is wrong.
C. Helping the person return to the right path with gentleness.
D. Using the person's shame to make sure he does not repeat the behaviour.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson calls for gentle restoration rather than shaming someone as a corrective response.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS II — [07:57]–[10:21] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Galatians 6:1 | Also cited in lesson segment: John 4

Q7. How did the Lesson explain the relationship between "you have put off the old man" and the instruction to "put off" the old man?
A. The two passages refer to two different old men operating at different stages of Christianity.
B. The old man has been put off as a spiritual provision, and the believer must partner by faith to see it in his life.
C. The old man is only considered put off after the believer has successfully stopped the deeds associated with him.
D. The instruction to put off the old man shows that the statement "you have put off" is describing a future reality.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes the provision in Christ from the believer’s practical response of faith.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [06:30]–[10:02] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Colossians 3; Ephesians 4; Jeremiah 31

Q8. What does Romans 7:22–23 demonstrate about the problem under the law?
A. The person did not delight in the law of God and therefore resisted it.
B. The law was not spiritual enough to overcome the desires of the flesh.
C. Another law in his members warred against the law of his mind.
D. The person understood the law but deliberately chose not to obey it.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson explains that an inner mechanism opposed the desire to follow God’s law.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [16:45]–[17:59] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 7:22

Q9. According to the Lesson, what does Romans 8:14 mean in its immediate context?
A. Those who are led by the Spirit will become sons of God.
B. Those who are sons of God are led by the Spirit of God.
C. Those who want to become sons must first learn to follow the Spirit.
D. Those who are spiritually mature are led by the Spirit, unlike other Christians.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson reads Romans 8:14 as describing the Spirit’s leading as characteristic of God’s sons.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [35:28]–[37:51] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 8:14 | Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 6

Q10. What does the statement "I'm kept, so I keep" communicate?
A. The believer keeps himself through discipline while the Spirit watches over his progress.
B. The Spirit keeps the believer, and the believer responds by yielding to the living of the Spirit.
C. The believer does not need to keep his body because the Spirit has already done everything.
D. The believer must keep his body before the Spirit can work in him.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson describes keeping the body as a partnership: the believer yields to the Spirit and acts accordingly.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [40:09]–[41:11] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 8:11; Colossians 3:1

Q11. A mature believer says, "I know my limits, so I can stay around this temptation." What does the Lesson challenge?
A. Self-assessment should not replace God's wisdom; when you can run, you should run.
B. Spiritual maturity should eventually make deliberate boundaries unnecessary.
C. The believer should remain in the situation long enough to prove that his discipline is genuine.
D. Exposure becomes dangerous only when temptation has already become strong.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson warns against overconfidence and advises avoiding unnecessary exposure when possible.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS IV — [02:01]–[03:09] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Timothy 2

Q12. Why does the lesson compare Esau's hunger with Jesus' forty-day fast?
A. To show that Esau lacked the biblical knowledge needed to recognise the seriousness of his decision.
B. To show that hunger weakens a person's ability to distinguish right from wrong.
C. To show that fasting gives a believer greater resistance to temptation than ordinary discipline can provide.
D. To show that the condition a person is in can affect his vulnerability so you must train for when defenses are down.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The comparison highlights that vulnerability can depend on a person’s condition, so preparation matters before defenses are weakened.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [03:47]–[06:12] (approximate range)

Q13. A believer breaks one destructive habit but soon begins depending heavily on another source of comfort. What does the Lesson suggest?
A. The believer needs stronger discipline because changing the source of pleasure is still a failure of restraint.
B. The new source has simply replaced the old temptation, showing that the first habit was never truly overcome.
C. The believer should remove the new source if it is becoming excessive, regardless of whether it is legitimate.
D. He may have changed the behaviour without addressing where he is looking for satisfaction.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson directs the believer to seek lasting satisfaction in God rather than relying on other sources of comfort.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS II — [02:02]–[03:47] and [06:09]–[06:59] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Jeremiah 2:13; John 4

Q14. Which best illustrates "wanting good things badly"?
A. A legitimate thing becomes excessive because the desire for it moves beyond its proper place.
B. A legitimate thing becomes dangerous simply because the believer enjoys it regularly.
C. A believer deliberately avoids a legitimate thing because he fears that enjoyment could become sinful.
D. A believer exercises restraint with a legitimate thing because he recognises that all pleasure must eventually be denied.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson explains that a legitimate good, such as food, can become sinful when pursued excessively.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [06:12]–[07:02] (approximate range)

Q15. What should be the believer's relationship with his mind and body?
A. His mind and body determine his spiritual identity but should gradually be brought under control.
B. His mind and body are irrelevant because only his spirit matters.
C. He is not his mind or his body therefore they are under control and subjected to the will of God.
D. His body is naturally controlled by the Spirit, while his mind must be controlled through human discipline.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson distinguishes the believer from the mind and body, and says they are to be brought under God’s will.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [48:47]–[50:00] and [57:13]–[58:47] (approximate ranges)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 12

Q16. According to the Lesson, what does a believer demonstrate when he walks in victory over sin?
A. That his personal discipline has become stronger than his previous habits.
B. That he has attained a higher level of Christianity.
C. That the resurrection of Jesus Christ has practical relevance in his life.
D. That his works have become sufficient for his acceptance before God.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson connects victory over sin with the practical relevance of Christ’s resurrection.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [34:01]–[35:28] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 6:4; Romans 8:14

Q17. Why can the believer "mortify" his members according to the Lesson?
A. Because mortification is what makes him dead to sin.
B. Because the practical action of mortifying follows the knowledge.
C. Because mortification causes the old man to become crucified with Christ.
D. Because the believer's ability to mortify depends on how strongly he feels the desire to resist sin.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says the believer’s practical action follows the spiritual reality of being dead to sin.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [41:11]–[43:21] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 8:11; Colossians 3:1; Romans 8:13

Q18. According to 2 Peter 1, why should the believer "give all diligence" if God has already given all things that pertain to life and godliness?
A. Because God's provision becomes effective only after the believer adds his own works to it.
B. Because the fact that God has already provided it is the very reason the believer can give all diligence.
C. Because the believer must complete what God began by supplying what was missing from the provision.
D. Because escaping the corruption in the world is dependent on human effort.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents God’s provision as the reason believers can diligently live it out, not something their effort must complete.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [45:37]–[47:48] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: 2 Peter 1

Q19. Why does the Lesson connect the revelation of grace with Romans 12?
A. Grace is meant to move the believer from what he has received into a practical response of presenting himself to God.
B. Grace first establishes doctrine, while presenting yourself to God introduces the separate discipline of Christian living.
C. Romans 12 shows that practical obedience becomes necessary when grace alone has not produced enough spiritual maturity.
D. The revelation of grace reduces the need for discipline because a believer who understands grace should naturally become transformed.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson links the teaching of grace to the practical response of presenting one’s body to God.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [00:16]–[01:05] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Titus 2:11 | Added from online research: Romans 12:1 (https://www.esv.org/verses/Rom%2012%3A1/)

Q20. Why can a recurring temptation become a "ticket to the next level"?
A. Successfully resisting repeated temptation demonstrates readiness for greater ministry responsibility.
B. Repeated temptation exposes weaknesses that, once removed, automatically produce spiritual promotion.
C. The presence of recurring temptation shows that God is preparing the believer for greater spiritual authority.
D. Overcoming it through the Word can strengthen the believer's capacity.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson teaches that overcoming temptation through the Word can strengthen the believer and contribute to spiritual growth.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS III — [04:31]–[06:54] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: James 1:3; James 1:2

Q21. A believer notices that certain movies repeatedly stir desires she later struggles to control. She stops watching them. What is this?
A. Avoiding temptation because mature believers should eventually be able to handle any environment.
B. Legalism, unless the content itself is clearly sinful.
C. A temporary measure that may protect her but does not actually train spiritual discipline.
D. Controlling exposure and building a structure that supports the outcome she wants.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson advises limiting exposure and using structures that support the desired outcome.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS IV — [01:08]–[04:06] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: 2 Timothy 2; James 1

Q22. Someone finds it difficult to give money even when he knows he should. From the Lesson, why can practising generosity become part of his training?
A. The discomfort of letting something go can become an opportunity to practise putting the flesh under.
B. His unwillingness to give reveals that the root of his other struggles is ultimately a lack of faith.
C. Giving is more powerful than all other disciplines because financial discipline controls other areas of the flesh.
D. His money must be brought under control first because attachment to possessions is the major cause of other forms of fleshly behaviour.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents giving, even when it feels difficult, as a way to practise putting the flesh under.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [10:47]–[11:30] (approximate range)

Q23. Which response best reflects "zoom out and zoom in"?
A. Focus on the wider discipline first, then return to the specific struggle once the broader weakness has been corrected.
B. Focus on the specific struggle because broader discipline can distract from the actual issue being addressed.
C. Replace the specific exercise with general spiritual disciplines because the specific behaviour is only a symptom.
D. Address the specific struggle while examining where the same lack of discipline may be appearing elsewhere.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson pairs targeted work on a specific struggle with attention to discipline in other areas.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [08:54]–[12:26] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Galatians 5:16

Q24. A believer prays in tongues, casts out demons, and attends church faithfully, yet repeatedly loses his temper. What does the Lesson tell us about this?
A. Those activities have not produced genuine spiritual maturity because anger is still there
B. He may be exercising spiritually without deliberately training the particular area where he is weak.
C. He needs to replace those activities with anger-focused exercises because general disciplines cannot address specific struggles.
D. His anger shows that his spiritual activities have become disconnected from the practical demands of Christian living.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson says general spiritual activity may not address a specific area that needs targeted training.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [01:05]–[02:54] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Titus 2:11

Q25. A believer is targeting a sexual habit and begins practising restraint with food, sleep and social media. Why can this help based on the Lesson?
A. These areas create the sexual temptation, so removing them removes the source of the struggle.
B. These pleasures are forms of fleshly gratification that must be brought under control before sexual discipline can develop.
C. Restraining the flesh in other areas can train the general capacity needed in the targeted area.
D. The believer is indirectly addressing the sexual habit because all forms of lack of discipline have the same immediate cause.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents self-restraint in other areas as general training that can strengthen discipline in a targeted struggle.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [09:42]–[10:47] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Galatians 5:16

Q26. A believer understands grace, defends it well, and listens to Lesson on it regularly, but his response to lusts doesn't change. What is he missing?
A. A stronger emphasis on spiritual gifts, since grace should first produce spiritual power.
B. A distinction between grace and holiness, since change comes later with growth.
C. More revelation, because practical obedience cannot be expected until the doctrine is fully understood.
D. The practical response grace is meant to produce which is denying ungodliness.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The lesson says the revelation of grace is meant to lead to a practical response, including denying ungodliness and worldly lusts.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [00:16]–[01:05] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Titus 2:11

Q27. According to the Lesson, what does the grace message include beyond the fact that sins are forgiven and not imputed?
A. That believers no longer need to be concerned about their conduct because grace covers every failure.
B. That the old man has been dealt with and believers are learning to walk consistently with the provision of Christ.
C. That believers should focus primarily on avoiding condemnation when they fall.
D. That practical holiness should be separated from the message of grace so that grace remains the focus.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The lesson includes both the old man being dealt with and learning to live consistently with Christ’s provision in its account of grace.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [53:22]–[55:07] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 5; Romans 6

Q28. Two believers pray, fast and study the Word. One struggles with anger; the other with pornography. What does the gym analogy require them to recognise?
A. The same spiritual exercises should eventually produce the same results, provided they are practised consistently.
B. Different struggles mainly require different levels of revelation.
C. Exercising spiritually does not mean the particular area that needs strengthening is being exercised.
D. Their common disciplines are insufficient because targeted struggles should be addressed separately from normal Christian disciplines.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson says general spiritual activity does not necessarily train the particular area where someone is struggling.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [01:05]–[02:54] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Titus 2:11

Q29. From the Lesson, why practise discipline in areas where you are not currently struggling?
A. Because learning to say "no" in ordinary areas can strengthen the capacity to say "no" when a greater temptation comes.
B. Because every area without strict control eventually becomes a spiritual weakness.
C. Because discipline in smaller matters gives a believer authority over stronger temptations.
D. Because the more disciplined a believer becomes generally, the less likely he is to experience serious temptation.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson presents restraint in ordinary areas as training for situations when a person is more vulnerable.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS I — [06:12]–[07:58] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Galatians 5:16

Q30. What best describes the accountability relationship taught in the Lesson?
A. Someone close enough to confront the believer, even if the confrontation creates shame that motivates change.
B. Someone with the same struggle who can therefore understand the believer's experience without needing to challenge him strongly.
C. Someone able to recognise when the believer is in trouble and respond firmly, respectfully and gently.
D. Someone who checks the believer's behaviour closely enough to prevent him from making another mistake.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson recommends someone who can recognize trouble and provide respectful, gentle accountability.
REF: HOW TO OVERCOME HABITS II — [08:46]–[10:21] (approximate range)
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Galatians 6:1

Q31. In Romans 1:16, how does the speaker describe what the gospel is?
A. A set of moral instructions that guide believers toward salvation
B. A message of forgiveness that leaves the believer's experience unchanged
C. The power of God unto salvation, demonstrated in men who believe
D. A covenant of rules that restrains people who already love God
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker reads Romans 1:16 and says the gospel is the power of God unto salvation, the power of God demonstrated in men.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [00:17]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 1:16

Q32. What detail does the speaker use to show that the Ephesians Paul prayed for were already born again?
A. Paul says they had completed a season of fasting before he wrote to them
B. Paul says they had already been ordained to lead the church at Ephesus
C. Paul addresses them as saints, faithful in Christ Jesus, and mentions their faith and love
D. Paul says they had already given up their former habits before he prayed
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker points to how the letter opens (to the saints at Ephesus and the faithful in Christ Jesus) and to Paul's thanks after hearing of their faith and love for all the saints.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [01:06; 01:45]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 1:16; Ephesians 1:15

Q33. According to the speaker, what is it that influences a believer's experience?
A. Spiritual facts about who he is in Christ
B. The intensity of his emotions during worship
C. The number of rules he is able to keep
D. The opinions of mature believers around him
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says spiritual facts about who you are in Christ are what influence your experience, which is why knowledge is the first important task.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [03:17]

Q34. A believer hears 'you are dead to sin' but points to his failures last night. How does the speaker say he should respond?
A. Take it into his spirit as revelation knowledge and adjust his experience to the Word
B. Treat the statement as a goal he will reach once his experience has improved
C. Accept it as head knowledge while trusting his experience as the better guide
D. Qualify the statement until it fits what he actually sees in his own life
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker ranks the Word above experience, says to get it into the spirit (not just head knowledge), and says to adjust your experience to the Word.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [04:23; 05:33]

Q35. What reasoning does the speaker give for why a Christian cannot have a demon?
A. Demons can only operate where believers have stopped praying
B. Demons lose their hold on a believer once he has fasted
C. A person indwelt by the Holy Ghost cannot be cohabited by a demon
D. Demons cannot enter anyone who has been baptized in water
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Recalling Pastor Chris's sermon, the speaker asks how a demon can cohabit a person who has the Holy Ghost indwelling the body.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [04:23; 05:33]

Q36. How does the speaker define 'that old man'?
A. An outside spirit that attacks believers who have neglected their prayer life
B. A list of sinful deeds that a believer must give up one by one in turn
C. The mechanism in fallen man that draws him irresistibly to consistent immorality
D. A stage of immaturity that every Christian eventually outgrows with time
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker describes the old man as the mechanism in the man who is not in Christ that draws him irresistibly to consistent immorality.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [06:30]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Colossians 3; Ephesians 4

Q37. From Colossians 3:9, what question does the speaker raise about the statement 'ye have put off the old man'?
A. If the mechanism behind lying has been put off, why must believers still be told not to lie?
B. If the old man was put off, why does Paul mention only lying and not other sins?
C. If believers must still avoid lying, why did Paul address them as saints?
D. If the old man was put off, why does Paul say this only to the Colossians?
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker asks why Paul tells people not to lie if the mechanism responsible for lying has been put off, since it should be automatic.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [07:58]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Colossians 3:9 | Also cited in lesson segment: Ephesians 4

Q38. According to E.W. Kenyon, as cited by the speaker, what two kinds of realities exist in God's provision in Christ?
A. Natural and supernatural realities
B. Positional and conditional realities
C. Legal and vital realities
D. Past and prophetic realities
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker cites E.W. Kenyon: the provision of God in Christ has legal and vital realities, spiritual facts one is meant to make his experience.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [07:58]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Colossians 3; Ephesians 4

Q39. What two points does the speaker say he will cover in the message?
A. Spiritual facts about victory over sin, then how to live consistently with them
B. The history of the old covenant, then the order of the Ten Commandments given
C. How to receive the Holy Spirit, then how to use the various spiritual gifts
D. The meaning of grace, then the ways a believer can earn God's continued favor
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker states two points: spiritual facts about victory over sin, and how to live in a manner consistent with that provision.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [08:55]

Q40. What point does the speaker make with the Lagos illustration about the new law on bikes?
A. A new law only matters where the authorities are present to enforce it
B. Old and new laws can be kept together if the new one is stricter
C. People may choose whichever law suits their situation best
D. If a new law is meant to replace the old, you cannot keep both
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: Using the Lagos bike law, the speaker argues that a new covenant meant to replace the old cannot be kept alongside it.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [12:53]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Jeremiah 31; Hebrews 8

Q41. In explaining Hebrews 8, where does the speaker place the fault that made a new covenant necessary?
A. With the priests, who failed to teach the law correctly
B. With the law, because its commands were unclear to the people
C. With the nation's leaders, who changed its terms over time
D. With the people, who did not continue in the covenant
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker says God found fault with the people (the law did not make anyone righteous), because they continued not in His covenant.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [14:14; 15:27]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Hebrews 8 | Also cited in lesson segment: Jeremiah 31; Romans 7

Q42. What does the speaker conclude from Jeremiah's statement that Israel 'continued not' in the covenant?
A. It could not help them continue in it, and righteousness is not attained by the law
B. The covenant was too long for the people to remember and obey faithfully over the years
C. Israel could keep the covenant only with the continued help of the prophets and priests
D. The covenant was withdrawn because it was too lenient with sin and rebellion
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the old covenant could not help them continue in it and that you can never attain a righteous status by doing the law.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [15:27]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Jeremiah 31; Hebrews 8; Romans 7

Q43. Why does the speaker quote 'I delight in the law of God' when explaining why Israel broke the old covenant?
A. To show that his delight in the law was enough to make him keep it
B. To show that delight in the law became possible only after the new covenant
C. To show that lack of interest in keeping the law was not the problem
D. To show that his interest in the law was the cause of his captivity
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker uses Romans 7:22 to answer those who say people broke the law because they did not want to keep it: interest was not the problem.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [16:45]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 7:22

Q44. What point does the speaker make with the illustration of a dog that discovers barking is a sin?
A. Laws can restrain a disposition but cannot change the nature behind it
B. Animals and people are judged by different standards of sin
C. A law becomes effective once its penalty is clearly announced
D. Sin depends on whether a creature knows that the law exists
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker says the best laws can do is restrain people who already have a disposition for evil, and they cannot change them.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [17:59]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Romans 7:22

Q45. From Romans 7:14, what does the speaker conclude about the law and the real problem?
A. The law is good but was only meant for an earlier generation
B. The law is spiritual and good; the problem is an inner mechanism in man
C. The law is flawed because it lacked the power to be kept
D. The law is spiritual but its rules were too many to follow
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker notes Paul calls the law spiritual and good, while the man is carnal and sold under sin, so the real problem is an inner mechanism.
REF: THAT OLD MAN — [19:19]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Romans 7:14

Q46. Which wilderness episode does the speaker use to show Israel already had a disposition toward what the commandments forbade?
A. Israelites turning away from Moses at the Red Sea
B. Hungry Israelites picking up stones to kill Moses
C. Israelites forgetting the commandments soon after leaving Egypt
D. Israelites refusing to follow Moses into the wilderness at all
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says that, though 'thou shalt not kill' was given, hungry Israelites in the wilderness picked up stones to kill Moses.

Q50. In Romans 8:3, how does the speaker say the new law at work in the believer came about?

Q77. What does the speaker draw from Paul's use of 'the fruit of the Spirit is' (singular) in Galatians 5?

EXPLANATION: The speaker notes it says 'is' and not 'are,' meaning the same Spirit has different tributaries or expressions, as the same flesh does.

Q78. What does the speaker's picture of water from the tap, the WC, and the shower all fed from one tank illustrate?

D. Fleshly struggles share one source, so attack them wholesomely at the source

EXPLANATION: The speaker says the fruits of the flesh come from the same source, so turning off one outlet at a time fails; attack it wholesomely at the main source.

B. Nobody told him to hide; shame comes with sin as part of the package
C. He hid because Eve had told him what she had done first
D. He hid only after God had confronted him about his act
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker says nobody had to tell Adam to hide himself; shame and sin go hand in hand, and shame can be used for good through accountability.
